findings.description: The component list now includes three review-catch-only arms, but Analysis.primaries() requires both hidden_test_pass_rate and defect_catch_rate for these arms. They cannot produce build-task pass-rate pairs.
findings.failure_mode: Even a complete, valid batch always produces 'no valid pair (hidden_test_pass_rate)' for these arms. Their decisions remain undecidable, making remove/simplify outcomes unreachable regardless of review results.
findings.suggested_fix: Add review-only primary selection using defect_catch_rate and apply it to arms restricted to review-catch.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: Excluding eval_only arms from components also removes a1_full_openmount from report rendering: detail_arms does not independently include evaluation-only arms.
findings.failure_mode: A batch can successfully collect the open-mount oracle control, but the report omits its results and its comparison with the closed-mount control. The newly declared oracle A/B therefore cannot be assessed from the report.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep eval_only arms excluded from shipped-default decisions and render their results and control comparisons in a separate evaluation section.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff adds three review-catch-only arms to `components` (via evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml lines 98-103), but Analysis.primaries() (ablation-report.py ~653-658, untouched) returns [hidden_test_pass_rate, defect_catch_rate] for any arm whose task_types contains review-catch; the suite rules' primaries_by_arm only has build_only / all_types, no review_only entry.
findings.description: a1_review_only, a1_no_dissent and a0_bare_fable are now decision components, but each is task_types: [review-catch] and so never produces a build row. primaries() will still demand a hidden_test_pass_rate pairing for them, so decide() records 'no valid pair (hidden_test_pass_rate)' and `decidable` is always false. The new AR test only asserts `decisions | length == 9`, which passes even though every one of the three new decisions is permanently undecidable; the report's k=9 EFP sentence then overstates the number of live comparisons.
findings.failure_mode: The sprint's stated purpose (deciding whether the AUDIT gate / review dissent earn their keep) can never yield remove/keep for the arms this PR adds; the report silently emits 'insufficient evidence' forever and the EFP line counts comparisons that cannot fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a review_only primaries rule (defect_catch_rate only) to the suite rules / primaries_by_arm and make primaries() select it when task_types == [review-catch]; extend the AR fixture so at least one of the new arms reaches a decidable state, and assert on its `line`, not just the count.

findings.description: The exclusion list is CONTROL, BARE, absent and eval_only. a0_bare_fable (loa_mount: false, phases: [BARE]) is a second bare baseline, not a shipped-default component, yet it is counted in `components`, gets a remove/keep decision line against a1_full, and inflates k in the expected-false-positive sentence (the new AR-12 expectation hard-codes k=9 including it).
findings.failure_mode: The report prints a nonsensical ship-default decision for a baseline arm and misreports the false-positive budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude arms whose toggles set loa_mount: false (or add an explicit `baseline: true` suite marker validated by validate-suite.sh) from `components`, and adjust AR-12 / the decisions-count assertion to 8.

findings.description: a1_full_openmount rows are accepted by the suite/arm checks and kept by the classifier, but the arm is now neither a component nor (per the untouched detail_arms list) a detail arm, so the open-mount oracle A/B that motivates eval_only has no rendering surface in the report at all.
findings.failure_mode: Operators run the eval_only arm in a batch and the resulting defect_catch_rate comparison against a1_full is silently dropped from report.md / report.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Render eval_only arms in a dedicated 'Evaluation controls (never decisions)' section paired against CONTROL on defect_catch_rate, or document that the oracle A/B is read from another tool.

findings.description: The dry run re-derives the sandbox .loa.config.yaml edits in an inline jq expression that mirrors lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles rather than calling it (or a shared table). Any future toggle added to apply_arm_toggles (the validator's TOGGLE_VALUES already lists karpathy_block, rule_files, audit_delta_instruction, context_resets, sprint_plan, which this jq does not report) makes `config_edits=` understate what the real run will change.
findings.failure_mode: Operators trust a dry-run plan that omits or misnames the config edits actually applied in the sandbox; the plan and the run diverge silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the toggle→config-key mapping into one function in lib/sandbox-mount.sh (e.g. `arm_config_edits <toggles-json>`) consumed by both apply_arm_toggles and the dry run, and add a test that compares the dry-run line to the keys apply_arm_toggles writes.

findings.cross_file_justification: The four arms are added to the suite file, but run-ablation.sh's default arm priority list (around line 55, untouched) and its --smoke default are not updated in this diff.
findings.description: A default batch (`--arms` unset) will never schedule a0_bare_fable, a1_review_only, a1_no_dissent or a1_full_openmount, so the new arms only run when an operator names them explicitly. Likewise, if run-ablation.sh has any pre-flight that calls pipeline-run.sh --dry-run outside run_trial, that call lacks LOA_ABLATION_BATCH_CONTEXT=1 and will exit 2 for the eval_only arm.
findings.failure_mode: The cycle-131 arms are silently absent from standard batches; the eval_only refusal may fire inside the runner if any non-run_trial invocation of pipeline-run.sh exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the three decision arms to the runner's default priority (and the eval_only arm to an explicit opt-in list), and grep run-ablation.sh for every `$PIPELINE_BIN` invocation to confirm run_trial is the only one.

findings.description: The new per-arm loop validates toggles, took_effect and eval_only but still does not reject duplicate arm ids. pipeline-run.sh selects ARM_DEF with a jq `select(.id == $arm)`; two arms sharing an id yield two JSON objects on separate lines, so `jq -c '.toggles // {}' <<<"$ARM_DEF"` produces two lines and the `jq -r '.eval_only // false'` test can never equal the single token `true`, which would let a duplicated eval_only arm slip past the refusal.
findings.failure_mode: A suite edit that accidentally duplicates an id passes validation and then produces malformed SUITE_TOGGLES / bypasses the eval_only guard at run time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `ids = [a.get('id') for a in arms]; for dup in {i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1}: bad('suite', f'duplicate arm id {dup}')` and, in pipeline-run.sh, assert ARM_DEF is exactly one JSON object (`jq -s length == 1`).

findings.description: c131_arms now loads the committed arm definitions, which changes a0_bare_fable's task_types from [all] (previous fixture) to [review-catch]. Any pre-existing Sprint 263 test in this file that runs a0_bare_fable against $BUILD will now hit pipeline-run.sh's task-type applicability check (the `jq -e --arg k "$KIND" --arg t "$TASK_TYPE"` branch) and be refused, failing the suite.
findings.failure_mode: Previously green bare_model_fable build-task tests fail with an applicability refusal after this fixture change.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep pipeline-run.bats for `a0_bare_fable "$BUILD"` / bare-fable build cases and either switch them to $REVIEWC or keep a separate fixture arm for the build-path bare_model test.
